items.docs: `defineFilters({ status: { kind: "options", label, options, multiple: true }, … })` is the whitelist: keys and wire `field` names must be identifiers, and nothing a person types becomes a field name. `FilterValues<typeof schema>` types the values. `toFilterAst(schema, values)` joins the active ones into a `FilterNode` (`and`, `or`, `not`, `{ field, op, value }`); text fields send `{ param: "q" }` by default (read with `searchTerms`) or match `{ fields, op: "contains" }`, joined by `or`. A date range's end is inclusive: `lte` the last day, or `end: "next-day"` for `lt` the day after when the backend stores date-times. `$where` adds an expression with groups, checked against `schemaFields(schema)`. Serializers, each its own module: `queryParams(ast, { style: "suffix" | "dto" | "bracket" })` (and only), `jsonAst` (POST body), `rsql`, `odata` (`$filter`), `springFilter` (turkraft), `graphqlWhere` (`dialect: "hasura" | "prisma"`) and `searchOnly`. Each escapes per its grammar and throws a `FilterSerializeError` for what it can't write safely, like a wildcard inside a text match. Dates are ISO 8601 by default (`dates: "iso" | "iso-date" | "epoch-ms" | fn`), from strings, `Date` or Temporal values. `matchesFilter(ast, item)` evaluates a filter in memory. `createUrlCodec(schema, { prefix, format, defaults })` keeps schema values, not the wire format, in readable params (`?status=open,closed&created=2026-01-01..2026-02-01&page=2&sort=name.asc`), one encoded `f` param when `$where` has groups, and drops anything a tampered URL puts there that doesn't fit. `parseFilterInput(field, input)` reads loose input (option labels, `"yes"`, `">= 10"`, `"2026-01-01..2026-01-31"`) into a field's value and `findFilterKey(schema, name)` finds a field by key or label, for agents and command palettes.

items.name: url-router
items.title: URL Router
items.description: A router adapter for blocks that keep state in the URL: read the location, navigate, build an href and follow changes. hashRouter keeps a hash route's path (#/devices?device=a1), historyRouter the path and query string, memoryRouter is for tests; wrap your own router's API in the same shape.
items.docs: A `UrlRouter` is `{ read(): { path, params }, navigate(to, { replace }), href(to), subscribe(listener) }`. `hashRouter()` reads `#/path?query`, changes the query without touching the path and builds `#/path?query` hrefs, which fast links follow as hash routes; `historyRouter()` does the same with `location.pathname` and `location.search` and keeps the hash on writes. Both keep `history.state` and notify each other. `memoryRouter("/settings")` records `entries` for tests. `withParam(location, name, value)` sets or removes one param. Pass a router to `createUrlParam(name, { router })` (`master-detail`, `settings-page`) or `routerUrlState(router)` (`url-state`). When your router has a contract of its own (a path segment like `#/devices/<id>`), wrap its API in this shape, or skip the adapter and control the block (`selectedId` and `onSelectedIdChange`, `currentSection` and `onSectionChange`) from the route.

items.name: url-param
items.title: URL Param
items.description: One value kept in the URL without knowing the router: the adapter master-detail and settings-page read, write and listen to, from location.search, a hash route's query or a UrlRouter.
items.docs: `createUrlParam(name, { in, router, history })` returns a `UrlParamAdapter` (`{ read(), write(value), subscribe(listener), href?(value) }`). By default it keeps the value in `location.search`; `{ in: "hash" }` in a hash route's query; `{ router }` goes through a `UrlRouter` from `url-router` (`hashRouter()`, `historyRouter()` or your router's own API). `history: "replace"` writes without a history entry. Pass it to `MasterDetail url` or `SettingsPage url`, or write your own adapter in the same shape.

items.name: url-state
items.title: URL State
items.description: Router-agnostic URL state: one UrlStateAdapter shape over the query string (historyUrlState), a hash router's query (hashUrlState) or memory (memoryUrlState), and useUrlState to read and write it.
items.docs: An adapter is `{ read(), write(params, { replace }), subscribe(callback) }`. `historyUrlState()` edits `location.search` with `replaceState` or `pushState` and follows `popstate`; `hashUrlState()` edits the query inside `#/route?…` and keeps the route; `memoryUrlState(initial)` keeps it in memory and records `history`, for tests and server rendering. A write through an adapter notifies its own subscribers too. `const [params, setParams] = useUrlState(adapter)` reads it with `useSyncExternalStore` (empty on the server) and writes with `replace` unless told otherwise. `routerUrlState(router)` goes through a `UrlRouter` from `url-router` (`hashRouter()`, `historyRouter()` or one over your router's API). Wrap your router's own API in the same shape to use it instead.

items.name: server-data
items.title: Server Data
items.description: React hooks for a PageSource on TanStack Query, behind signatures of their own: useServerPage, useServerTotal, useServerInfinite, useServerQuery, useInvalidateSource, usePatchSource, useHoldSource, useSourceMutation and usePageController, with DataProvider and createDataClient for the defaults.
items.docs: `useServerPage(source, request)` loads one page with the query key `[...source.key, "page", filter, sort, position, size]`: the previous rows stay while the next page loads (`previous`), a superseded request is aborted through its signal, and it returns `items`, `status` (`pending`, `error`, `success`), `fetching`, `total`, `navigation`, `error` and `retry`. When the source has `fetchTotal`, `useServerTotal` counts beside it, a query of its own that never holds the rows back. `useServerInfinite(source, { filter, sort, size })` adds page after page (`loadMore`, `hasMore`, `loadingMore`) by page number or cursor. `useServerQuery(key, fetch, { enabled, staleTime, placeholder, keepPrevious, select, seeds })`, from `use-server-query`, loads one resource that isn't paged (a detail, a snapshot, a short list) and returns `data`, `status`, `fetching`, `previous`, `error` and `retry`; `fetch({ signal })` is aborted when the key changes or nothing reads it, and a key under the source's (`[...tasks.key, "detail", id]`) lets the hooks below reach it. `select` picks what `data` holds (TanStack's `select`: memoised, structurally shared, typed as its result). `defineResource({ key, fetch, staleTime, seeds })` declares a resource once for every screen that reads it, through `useServerResource(resource, params, options)`; `seeds: (data) => [other.seed(params, value)]` writes other resources from an answer, mounted or not, unless the fetch was aborted or that resource got data after the fetch started. `error` is `unknown`, or the `defaultError` registered with TanStack's `Register`, or the type parameter after the data type; the page, infinite, total and mutation hooks take it too. `useInvalidateSource(source, { throwOnError })` refreshes everything under the source's key and resolves once the shown queries reloaded; with `throwOnError` (on the hook or per call) a failed reload rejects, for a toast. `useSourceMutation({ mutationFn, source, optimistic })` refreshes it once the change settles, and `optimistic: (items, variables) => items` shows the change at once and restores the rows if it fails. To write the server's answer instead of refreshing, `settleItems: (items, result, variables) => items` maps the rows of every page and infinite query under the key (totals stay) and `settle: (result, variables, current, queryKey) => data` writes every `useServerQuery` under it (`undefined` leaves one alone): they reach every cached query under the key, mounted or not, each written query's read in flight is cancelled first, nothing is requested, and the rest of the key is marked stale (a read of it already in flight starts again). A failed mutation refreshes the key unless `refreshOnError: false`. Every reload these hooks make (`useInvalidateSource`, a mutation's refresh after success or failure, the restart after `settle`) starts any read in flight under the key again, its first load included, since it may answer with the data from before the write: the old request's signal aborts, the query stays pending or fetching without an error, and its late answer or AbortError is dropped (TanStack's `invalidateQueries` joins a first load instead). `usePatchSource(source)` returns `patch({ items, resource }, { refetch, throwOnError })` for a change the app learned of elsewhere (a push event, another request's answer): `items(rows)` maps every page and infinite query under the key (totals stay) and `resource(current, queryKey)` every other query (`undefined` leaves one alone), mounted or not, without a request; a read in flight whose query it writes, and any first read (no data to patch yet), is cancelled silently and started again in the same batch, with or without `refetch`, so its answer from before the change never lands and nothing stays pending; `refetch: true` also reloads the key and resolves once the shown queries reloaded; `inFlight: "cancel"` stops a written query's read instead, and `awaitRestarted` waits for the restarted reads. The call resolves with `{ written, cancelled, restarted, refetched }`, the query keys it wrote, whose read it stopped, whose read it started again, and that its reload read, so a screen can tell whether a read ran. `patchSource(client, source, changes, options)` does the same outside React. `useHoldSource(source)` returns a function that begins a hold, `holdSource(client, source)` outside React: it cancels every read in flight under the key now and pauses the hooks' reads under it (they show as fetching and send nothing) until `hold.patch(changes, options)` writes the caller's own answer and ends it, a written query's paused read dropped, or `hold.release()` ends it without writing, and the paused reads run; the hook releases its holds on unmount. `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `refetchOnReconnect` and `refetchOnMount` (`true` when stale, `"always"`, `false`) set when a query reloads on its own: defaults on `createDataClient` (no reload on focus; stale queries on mount, and on reconnect unless `networkMode` is `always`), per hook on `useServerQuery`, `defineResource`, `useServerResource` (the call wins over the definition), `useServerPage`, `useServerInfinite` and `useServerTotal`. Never reload a resource whose reads overwrite per-item ETags a later write sends back: turn focus and reconnect off on its `defineResource`, since any reader that asks reloads it for all. `scope: { id }` runs mutations with the same id one at a time in call order, across hooks, each after the one before has settled (its refresh included); a failure doesn't stop the queue, so to stop at the first one set a flag in `onError` that `mutationFn` checks. `mutationKey` finds them with `useMutationState`. `usePageController(source, options)` keeps a `createPageController` for the component's life and follows the URL while mounted. The hooks use the app's `QueryClient` when one is provided; otherwise a shared default, so nothing has to be mounted. `DataProvider` provides one with `createDataClient` defaults when the app has none: two retries except on a 4xx (read from the error's `status`), 30 s fresh, no refetch on window focus. `createDataClient({ retry, retryDelay })` takes a number of retries (the 4xx rule stays), `false` (none) or a rule `(failures, error) => boolean`, and `isTransientError(error)` (a network TypeError, 408, 425, 429 or 5xx) writes the usual one: `retry: (failures, error) => failures < 3 && isTransientError(error)`; mutations never retry. `networkMode` (`online`, `always`, `offlineFirst`) on `createDataClient` sets queries and mutations, and every hook (`useServerQuery`, `defineResource`, `useServerResource`, `useServerPage`, `useServerInfinite`, `useServerTotal`, `useSourceMutation`) takes its own: TanStack's default, `online`, pauses reads after the browser's `offline` event, so a page never reaches its error state; use `always` for a local backend (Electron IPC, localhost) or an app with its own offline UI. Results reach React through TanStack's `notifyManager`, one `setTimeout(0)` after a query settles, so a test that awaits a single `act()` can see the state before it: call `notifyManager.setScheduler(queueMicrotask)` in the test setup, or wait with `findBy`/`waitFor`. With server rendering, mount a `DataProvider` per request. `useDelayedFlag(active, episode)` turns true once a load has taken 400 ms, for a status that says "Loading…" only when it matters, and `useReachEnd(onReach, enabled)` is a ref that runs `onReach` when an element scrolls into view, for infinite lists.

items.name: server-data-table
items.title: Server Data Table
items.description: A DataTable over a PageSource: the server filters, sorts and pages; page numbers, previous and next, or load more follow what the source gives; DataState covers loading, error with retry and empty; a polite status says "Showing 21–40 of 312" after each load; filters, sort and page can live in the URL.
items.docs: `<ServerDataTable label source columns filters labels={{ errorTitle, retry, emptyTitle }} />`. Columns are DataTable columns; `sortField` sorts one on the server, and `sortMode="multi"` adds a column with Shift+click. `navigation="auto"` shows page numbers with an exact total (or the source's `fetchTotal`), previous and next with an estimate or only `hasMore`, and load more for a cursor; `"infinite"` also loads when the end scrolls into view, beside the button. `pageSize` (25) and `pageSizes` (`[10, 25, 50, 100]`, capped by the source's `maxPageSize`) show a page size select. `filters` takes a `defineFilters` schema, `filterUi` picks the built-in filter UI: `"search"` (a `FilterSearch`, the default when the schema has a text field), `"chips"` (search and `FilterChips`) or `"panel"` (search and a `FilterPanelTrigger` that opens a `FilterPanel` beside the table, a bottom sheet on narrow screens), and `toolbar` composes your own from the parts. `urlState={hashUrlState()}` (or `historyUrlState()`, or `{ adapter, prefix, history, format }`) keeps filters, sort and page in readable params, and Back and Forward move through them. While a page loads its predecessor stays, marked `aria-busy`; it never shows empty while loading or after an error. The status says "Loading…" only once a load has taken 400 ms, and focus stays on the control pressed. Agents sort and page through the table (`sortBy`, `setPage`) and filter through the "{label} filters" group: `filter("Status", ["Open"])`, `clearFilters()`. Visible copy has no default: `errorTitle`, `retry` and `emptyTitle` are required; `labels.searchPlaceholder` writes the search box's placeholder ("Search {label}…"), control names default to English (`labels.pageSize`, `loadMore`, `range`…), and the page navigation is named "{label} pages" (`labels.pagination`) so two tables on a page keep distinct landmarks. Pass `controller` from `usePageController` to drive it from outside. Counts ("Showing 1,001–1,020 of 12,345"), the page sizes and the chips' numbers and dates follow the page's `<html lang>` through `useLocale`; `locale` overrides it, and `labels.range` receives it.

items.name: server-list
items.title: Server List
items.description: A List over a PageSource that grows as you scroll: ListItem rows, virtualized past 200, one tab stop with row navigation, the next page when the end comes into view, and a visible Load more button for keyboards and agents.
items.docs: `<ServerList aria-label source renderItem itemText labels={{ errorTitle, retry, emptyTitle }} />`, with `renderItem` returning a `ListItem`. It pages with `useServerInfinite`, by page number or cursor, `pageSize` (50) rows at a time. With `infinite` (default) the next page loads as the end of the list scrolls into view; the Load more button is always there too, so keyboards and agents reach every page, and it keeps focus while it loads and once there is no more. `DataState` covers loading, error with retry and empty, the list is `aria-busy` while a new search loads, and a polite status says "Showing 1–50 of 312" after each load ("Loading…" only past 400 ms). `filters` takes a schema (a `FilterSearch` by default, or your own `toolbar`), and the `List` props (`variant`, `value`, `onValueChange`, `onSelect`, `virtualize`, `estimateSize`) pass through. Agents select rows through the list's `select(id)` and press Load more. Its counts follow `<html lang>` through `useLocale`; `locale` overrides it.

items.name: git-chip
items.title: Git Chip
items.description: Inline chips for git names in text: GitFileChip (a file icon and the path in mono) and GitBranchChip (a branch icon and the name).
items.docs: `<GitFileChip path="src/routes.ts" />` and `<GitBranchChip name="main" />` sit inline in a sentence, like a commit message: quiet tokens in caption mono, no taller than the line, with a size-3 icon and muted text on a translucent fill that shows on a hovered or selected row as on the card (an outline appears only in forced-colors mode). `textRef` renders the name empty for a virtualizer's `findableText`. Both take `render` and any span prop.

items.name: repository-select
items.title: Repository Select
items.description: A select for one git repository out of several: the trigger shows the name, each option its path, the branch checked out and its state (uncommitted, ahead, behind, no remote, up to date). On UI SDK Select, so keyboard, typeahead and agents work as in any select.
items.docs: `<RepositorySelect aria-label="Repository" repositories={[{ value: "api", name: "api", path: "~/work/acme/api", branch: "main", uncommitted: 0, ahead: 0, behind: 0, remote: true }]} value={repo} onValueChange={setRepo} />`. Each repository is `{ value, name, path?, branch?, uncommitted?, ahead?, behind?, remote?, disabled? }`; `ahead`/`behind` are `null` without an upstream and `remote: false` shows "No remote". The state reads as badges: uncommitted (warning), ahead (info), behind (outline), No remote (secondary), or Up to date (success) when none apply. Typeahead matches `name`; the trigger shows it alone. `size="sm"` fits a header, like `CommitHistory headerStart`. Every word is in `labels` (`uncommitted(n)`, `ahead(n)`, `behind(n)`, `noRemote`, `upToDate`). Takes every Select prop but `items`, `options` and `multiple`, plus `triggerProps` and `contentClassName`.

items.name: commit-graph
items.title: Commit Graph
items.description: The model behind CommitHistory: commits, a one-pass nesting of merged branches under their merge, the rows that show with merges open or closed, git log --graph style lanes laid out lazily, and a commit message parser for file and branch chips.
items.docs: `createCommitGraph(commits)` reads commits newest first, children before parents (`git log --topo-order`), once: each merge's merged-in branch nests under it as the block of commits right after it that only it reaches. `updateCommitGraph(previous, commits)` reuses the previous graph when the history only grew at the end (an older page) or only changed content (a pending commit that finished), so a page costs its own rows. `visibleRows(graph, expanded)` skips closed merges' blocks; `createLaneLayout(graph, visible, { maxLanes })` gives each shown row its node's lane and the lanes running into, out of and past it, computed the first time a row (or one below it) is asked for and kept; an octopus merge's parents past `maxLanes` count as `overflow`. `parseCommitMessage` turns backticked paths into file segments, `` `branch:name` `` into branch segments and git's merge subjects ("Merge a into b") into branch chips; `commitSubject` reads a message as plain text and `createCommitFinder(graph)` finds a commit by id, hash prefix or subject. `createBranchModel(graph, branches, { base, staleAfter })` works out each branch's commits ahead of the base along its first parent, its merge-base, how far behind it is and whether it's active, stale or merged, in O(commits + commits ahead), and gives each a stable lane colour (`tag`). For the branches view, `createLaneLayout` takes `reserve` (the base's head on lane 0), `headTag` (a head's lane colour), `keepLanes` (a branch keeps its lane down to its merge-base) and `maxLanes`, past which lanes are counted in `hidden` rather than drawn; a row costs O(maxLanes + parents) however many lanes are open.

items.name: commit-history
items.title: Commit History
items.description: A commit trail, one line per commit: a graph lane down the side, merges collapsed to one row that open their branch on a curved side lane, a pending commit that spins until it lands, and a commit's details inline under its row. Virtualized for 50,000+ commits; agents read and act on commits by name.
items.docs: `<CommitHistory aria-label commits branch branches onBranchChange />`. `commits` are newest first in `git log --topo-order` order, each `{ id, parents, message, date, author?, hash?, body?, tags?, stats?, status? }`; a string message turns backticked paths into `GitFileChip`s and git's merge subjects into `GitBranchChip`s, or pass segments. Merges start collapsed: a chevron, and a press, Enter, Right/Left or `expanded`/`defaultExpanded`/`onExpandedChange` open the merged commits on a side lane that curves back at the fork point. A press or Enter on any other commit opens its details under the row (author, the date in the page's language, the short hash with a copy button, files and +/- lines in success and destructive, the body); `detailsMode="multiple"` keeps several open, `details`/`defaultDetails`/`onDetailsChange` control them, and `onOpenCommit` takes the press instead, for apps that navigate to a commit. While details are open the other rows dim to `muted-foreground` (4.5:1); `focusMode` forces it on or off. `status: "pending"` spins a hollow ring and shows `labels.pending` in the link colour in place of the time; when it turns `"done"` the node grows into its check and the time and tags fade in. The header counts finished commits, or `count`. `tags` are `Badge`s with a `tone`; the time is `formatElapsed` ("26m") with the full date as its title, and every row's name reads "Merge invoice-pdf into main, 38 minutes ago, Release". One `useNow` clock every 30 s, or pass `now`. Rows virtualize with variable heights (open details are measured), the graph is laid out lazily from the top and an appended page costs only its rows; `hasMore`, `loadingMore` and `onLoadMore` load older commits as the end scrolls into view and from a Load more button. Give the history a bounded height (`className="max-h-[32rem]"` or a flex parent) so it scrolls itself. `findable` lets find in page reach commits scrolled out of view, by subject: rows move to UI SDK's virtualizer, whose findable layers are built once the page is idle after its first paint, and a match scrolls its row into view and highlights it in the row. It's off by default because it costs: on 50,000 commits about a frame on some held-arrow presses (p95 22–27 ms against 10 ms) and 10–40% on the first paint; with it the scroller is capped at `--commit-history-height` (40rem). Agents get `expandDetails`, `collapseDetails`, `expand`, `collapse`, `copyHash` (it returns the hash), `openCommit` (with `onOpenCommit`) and `selectBranch`, each taking a commit's id, hash or subject. `labels` overrides every text; `controller` from `createCommitHistoryController()` drives it from outside. `view="branches"` shows every active branch at a glance, a compact `git log --graph --all` (commits in `--all --topo-order`): `branches` takes `{ name, head, tone?, ahead?, behind?, updatedAt?, author? }`, the base (`branch`) keeps lane 0, each unmerged branch runs in its own lane from its merge-base in a stable chart colour (or its `tone`) and is labelled at its head with a pill (name, ↑ahead ↓behind, read in the row's name: "branch feature/x, 3 ahead, 12 behind"); merged branches stay folded under their merge. The header select lists the active branches under "All branches", each with a dot in its lane's colour (also in the trigger), its name, arrows for ahead and behind (a zero side left out, the words for screen readers) and its last update, and a search field filters them by name (`labels.searchBranches`, `labels.noBranches` when none match): choosing one, pressing its pill in the trail, or `focusBranch(name)` scrolls to its head and focuses it, and with `filterBranch` shows only the base and that branch; pressing the pill again shows them all. Past `maxLanes` (8 in this view) lanes collapse into "+N". Agents also get `focusBranch` and the read-only `listBranches()` (name, head, ahead, behind, updatedAt, state). 50,000 commits with 200 branches lay out in linear time.

items.name: server-commit-history
items.title: Server Commit History
items.description: A CommitHistory over a PageSource: older commits load as the end scrolls into view and from a Load more button, the header counts the source's total, and the graph carries on across pages.
items.docs: `<ServerCommitHistory aria-label source filter labels={{ errorTitle, retry, emptyTitle }} />` inside a `DataProvider`. `source` is any `PageSource<Commit>` (`cursorSource` for a `git log` API that returns a cursor, `pagedSource`, or `arraySource` in memory) and `filter` what it filters on, like `{ branch }`: a new filter starts again from the newest commit. `pageSize` (100) commits per request through `useServerInfinite`; `DataState` covers loading, error with retry and empty. Every other `CommitHistory` prop passes through.

items.name: git-tree
items.title: Git Tree
items.description: A repository's files at a commit on UI SDK's Tree: folders first with lucide icons, changed files marked added, modified, deleted or renamed in their tone, folders that hold a change marked too. Virtualized for 100,000 files; agents open and expand by path.
items.docs: `<GitTree aria-label files onOpenFile current />`. `files` are paths (strings, a trailing `/` for an empty folder) or `{ path, status, from }` with `status` one of `added`, `modified`, `deleted`, `renamed`; the tree is UI SDK's `treeFromPaths`, so folders sort first. A changed file shows a one-letter mark (`labels.mark`) and its icon in the status tone, and its name reads "proration.ts, Modified" ("pdf.ts, Renamed, from src/invoice/print.ts"); folders that hold a change carry a dot and "Has changes". Folders with changes start open; `expanded`/`defaultExpanded`/`onExpandedChange` control them. Arrows, Home/End, typeahead and Left/Right come from UI SDK's Tree; a press or Enter on a file calls `onOpenFile(path)`, and `current` marks the file shown elsewhere. Rows virtualize (only those in view render, every one stays reachable by keyboard and agents); give it a bounded height. `findable` lets find in page reach files and folders out of view, by name, through UI SDK's findable layers built once the page is idle; off by default, as it costs up to a frame on some held-arrow presses at 100,000 files (p95 about 16 ms against 10 ms), and it caps the scroller at `--git-tree-height` (40rem). Agents get `open(path)` (a file, opening its folders first, or a folder), `expand(path)` and `collapse(path)`. Built on UI SDK's Tree directly; once a styled `tree` item ships, its rows can reuse it.

items.name: filter-search
items.title: Filter Search
items.description: The search box of a filter schema: shows the text at once and commits it after the page controller's 250 ms debounce, Enter commits, Escape clears. FilterScope gives filter UIs their schema and controller and lets agents filter by a field's label.
items.docs: Inside a `ServerDataTable` (its `toolbar`, or `filterUi="search"`) it finds the schema and controller by itself; elsewhere wrap filter UIs in `<FilterScope schema controller label>` or pass `schema` and `controller`. It edits the schema's first text field and takes its `label` as its name unless you pass one; its placeholder is `placeholder`, or the scope's `searchPlaceholder` (a `ServerDataTable` sets "Search {label}…"). An agent's `setValue` commits without the debounce. `FilterScope` is a group named by `label` with agent actions `filter(field, value)`, where the field is a key or a label and the value loose input (option labels or values, `"yes"`, `">= 10"`, `"2026-01-01..2026-01-31"`, read by `parseFilterInput`), and `clearFilters()`. `useFilterScope(props)` returns the schema, controller and state for a filter UI of your own.

items.name: filter-chips
items.title: Filter Chips
items.description: Filters as chips in a FilterBar: one chip per active filter that opens an editor for its field, a button that removes it, Add filter for the others, and reset. Picks apply at once; typed values on Enter or when the editor closes.
items.docs: Inside a `ServerDataTable` with `filterUi="chips"`, or a `FilterScope`, it reads the schema and controller (or pass `schema` and `controller`). Each chip's text is its name, "Status: Open, Blocked" (`labels.chip`, with `summarizeFilter` for the value), and opens a popover with the field's `FilterField`; a choice applies at once, a typed text or number on Enter or when the popover closes. Its remove button, "Remove Status filter", clears the field and returns focus to Add filter, a menu of the fields without a value: choosing one opens its editor, and leaving it empty adds nothing. The toolbar is one tab stop with arrow keys (UI SDK Toolbar), named by `labels.toolbar`, and Reset filters shows while any chip applies. `fields` limits and orders the fields offered (every field but the search field by default); `valueLabels` names remote option ids it hasn't loaded. Labels default to English and can be overridden. Numbers and dates in the chips ("Jan 1, 2026 – Jan 31, 2026", a date-only value read as the day it names) and in the editors follow `<html lang>` through `useLocale`; `locale` overrides it.

items.name: filter-panel
items.title: Filter Panel
items.description: Every filter of a schema in one form, applied together: a SidePanel beside the results on wide screens, a bottom Drawer sheet on narrow ones; Apply and Reset.
items.docs: `<FilterPanel open onOpenChange />` inside a `FilterScope` (or with `schema` and `controller`), toggled by `<FilterPanelTrigger open onOpenChange count />`, which shows how many filters apply (`countActiveFilters`). `ServerDataTable filterUi="panel"` puts both in place. Each field is a `FilterField` editing a draft; Apply (a submit button, so Enter works) sends it, Reset clears the fields the panel shows and applies at once. It is a `SidePanel` with `narrow="sheet"`: at 760px and below a modal bottom sheet that Apply closes; wider, non-modal beside the results, staying open, closing on Escape and returning focus to `returnFocus`. The draft starts again whenever the applied filters change elsewhere, like a chip or the URL. `labels` names the title, Apply, Reset and Close, in English by default.

items.name: filter-field
items.title: Filter Field
items.description: The control for one filter schema field, named by its label: an input for text, a select or checkboxes for options, a select for a boolean, a comparison and numbers, date pickers, or a ServerCombobox for remote options.
items.docs: `<FilterField field={schema.status} value onValueChange />` is controlled with the field's value type (`FilterValues`); an empty choice gives `undefined`. Options are a `Select` with Any, or a checkbox group when `multiple`; a boolean a `Select` of `trueLabel` and `falseLabel`; a number a Comparison `Select` (`operators`, `eq`, `gte`, `lte` and `between` by default) and a Value `NumberInput`, side by side once the container is 20rem wide, Minimum and Maximum for between; a date a `DatePicker`, a range two labelled From and To (each end optional); a remote option a `ServerCombobox` that says Any until something is chosen, which reports chosen labels through `onValueLabels`. `appliesAtOnce(field)` says whether a change is a pick or typing. `FilterChips` and `FilterPanel` use it; use it in a form of your own. Every control has a visible label. `labels` translates Any, Yes, No, From, To, Comparison, Value, Minimum, Maximum and the comparisons. Date pickers and number inputs take `locale`, or follow `<html lang>` through `useLocale`.

items.name: server-combobox
items.title: Server Combobox
items.description: A Combobox whose options come from a PageSource, searched on the server as you type: requests wait for typing to pause and are aborted when replaced, the next page loads at the end of the list, and the server's order is kept. With multiple, choices show as chips.
items.docs: `<ServerCombobox source getLabel value onValueChange />` inside a `Field` with a `FieldLabel`. The source's filter gets the typed text as `q`; `getValue` picks what an option stores (the source's `getId` by default). It runs on UI SDK's `useAsyncOptions` with `filter={false}`: `debounce` (250 ms) before a search, the previous options kept while the next load, the request it replaces aborted, and `pageSize` (20) more whenever scrolling or the arrow keys reach the last option, by page number or cursor. `multiple` keeps an array and shows each choice as a chip with a remove button named "Remove {label}"; `valueLabels` names values chosen before their options load, such as ids read from the URL. A hidden status announces loading, errors and the count; `labels` translates it and the control names. Agents choose an option by its label. The count follows `<html lang>` through `useLocale`; `locale` overrides it.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: Recharts v3 composed with Eskais tokens: ChartContainer maps a config to --color-<key> variables (light and dark), popover tooltips and legends, and ChartDataTable renders the same data as a table for screen readers and agents. The container is a figure that requires a name.
items.docs: Categorical series use --chart-1 to --chart-5. Series with a meaning use the series tokens, which follow the theme and meet 3:1 on the background and card in both modes: --series-positive (gains, done; from --success), --series-negative (losses, failures; from --destructive), --series-target (a goal or reference line; from --foreground) and --series-remaining (what is left, a track; from --muted-foreground over --muted). Pass them as a config color, e.g. { done: { label: "Done", color: "var(--series-positive)" } }, or use the Tailwind colours (stroke-series-target). Don't rely on colour alone: add a legend or labels, and dash a target line. `ChartDataTable data labelKey keys` is generic over the row type (`TRow extends object`), so rows typed by an `interface` pass as they are and `labelKey` and `keys` must name their fields.

items.name: lightbox
items.title: Lightbox
items.description: A UI SDK Dialog that shows one image of a set: previous and next (buttons and arrow keys), a counter, the caption, an open-original link and fit or actual size. Dark variants follow the theme with no flash; agents get next, previous and goTo.
items.docs: Pass `items` ({ id, src, srcDark?, alt, name?, href? }) and control `open`/`onOpenChange` and `index`/`onIndexChange`, or put a `DialogTrigger` inside as children. `srcDark` is rendered next to `src` and CSS shows it under `.dark` or the system dark preference (unless `<html>` opts into light), so there is no flash. Focus returns to the trigger, or to whatever was focused when it opened; pass `finalFocus` to override. The dialog is sized in % of the top layer, never viewport units. Labels are English and overridable through `labels`. Agents see `Image viewer` with `next`, `previous` and `goTo(index)` (0-based).

items.name: image-cropper
items.title: Image Cropper
items.description: UI SDK ImageCropper styled: a selection that dims the rest of the image with a grid while dragging and eight handles, or a round frame the image pans and zooms under, with zoom, rotate and flip, and cropImage.
items.docs: `<ImageCropper aria-label src alt aspectRatio mode shape maxZoom crop onCropChange onCropCommit>`: with no children it renders the viewport (the image's ratio, or a square frame), the image, a selection that dims the rest through a spread `--overlay` shadow, shows a grid at the thirds while dragging and has eight handles (none in `mode="frame"`), then a zoom slider and Rotate, Flip horizontally and Flip vertically buttons with icons and their names from `labels`. Rotate and flip show their label because they're disabled until the image loads, when a tooltip couldn't show. `cropImage(src, crop, { width, shape })` (re-exported) makes the file; save in `onCropCommit`. In UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.12 the handles sit inside the selection's slider, which axe reports as nested-interactive; a frame has no handles.

items.name: image-scan
items.title: Image Scan
items.description: An image under analysis, from a controlled status: a preview, a scan (a turning sweep or a progress line over the image, a progress bar, steps and Cancel), the detected regions as buttons over the image with a legend, or an error with Retry. Announces each change; agents get scan, cancel, retry and selectRegion.
items.docs: `<ImageScan src alt width height status progress statusText steps step regions selectedRegion onSelectedRegionChange onScan onCancel onRetry error fit aspectRatio legend actions labels>`: `status` is `uploaded`, `scanning`, `result` or `error`, and you drive it. While scanning, `progress` (0 to 1) makes the bar and a line over the image determinate; without it a wedge turns over the image. Both are transforms on the compositor, and reduced motion keeps only the bar and a still frame. `regions` are `{ id, label, box: { x, y, width, height }, description?, tone? }` with the box in fractions of the image from its top left corner (physical, so right to left doesn't mirror it); they render in reading order as toggle buttons over the image, named by their label, and in a legend below (pointer only, `aria-hidden`). The frame keeps the image's ratio (`width`/`height`, or the loaded image's), or `aspectRatio` with `fit` `contain` or `cover`, and the boxes follow the drawn image in CSS from the frame's container units; `mapRegionBox(box, { fit, image, frame })` gives the same rectangle in pixels. Screen readers hear `labels.scanning`, progress at most every tenth and two seconds (`labels.progress`), `labels.found(count)`, and the error at once. Cancel, Retry and Scan show when their handler is set; agents see `status` and the regions as items, and call `scan`, `cancel`, `retry` and `selectRegion(id or label)`; a call outside its state (or for a region that isn't there) throws, so the step fails with the reason.

items.name: model-viewer
items.title: Model Viewer
items.description: A 3D model (glTF or GLB) in a stage that turns with drag, wheel, pinch and keys, with views, zoom, reset, animation clips, morph weights (a Float32Array aligned with the target names, or by name) and ARKit expressions eased in the render loop, and an optional floor (a grid, a contact shadow) in the theme's colours. A new model fades in over the old one, keeping its weights. controls="gestures" keeps drag and keys without the bar, for controls of your own through handleRef and useModelViewerControls. The three.js scene (react-three-fiber) is a separate chunk, loaded when the stage nears the viewport and only with WebGL; a poster stands in until then and without WebGL. Agents get rotate, zoom, reset, setView, play, pause and selectClip.
items.docs: `<ModelViewer model alt poster summary aspectRatio view defaultView onViewChange framing clip defaultClip onClipChange playing defaultPlaying onPlayingChange loop speed weights targetNames expressions material background floor autoRotate controls handleRef load overlay sceneChildren onLoad onError error labels>`: `model` is a URL, its bytes (an ArrayBuffer) or a loaded scene (`{ scene, animations }`). The stage is `role="img"` named by `alt`, described by the keyboard hint and the visible `summary`; while it has focus, arrows turn the model, + and - zoom and Home resets. Views are `front`, `three-quarter`, `side` and `back`; free rotation sets the view to `null`. `framing` is `"full"` or a sphere of the model (`{ center: [x, y, z], radius }` in its own units), like a face for a close-up. `weights` are morph weights: a Float32Array (or numbers) aligned with `targetNames`, which default to the GLB's `extras.targetNames` (meshes in scene order), or a map by name; values aren't clamped, so a principal component can be negative. `expressions` maps ARKit names (`mouthSmileLeft`) to weights on the `expr.<name>` targets, over `weights`. They ease inside the render loop with no allocation and no React render per frame; a target never set is left to clips. A new `model` loads under the shown one and takes over its camera, weights and clip time: it replaces it at once when the two look the same (meshes, vertex counts, targets, colours), or fades in over it. `playing` left out (or `null`) plays the clip once loaded, except under reduced motion, which also drops auto-rotation and turns every camera move and swap into a jump. `material="toon"` swaps in a three-tone toon material. `floor` draws a grid disc and a contact shadow under the model's feet in the theme's muted foreground, and pools the card colour over the stage. `controls` is `true` (the bar under the stage, and drag, wheel, pinch and keys), `"gestures"` (the gestures and keys without the bar) or `false` (a still stage); with `"gestures"`, `handleRef` hands over the viewer's handle and `useModelViewerControls(handle)` its status, view, clips and playing, rendering only when one changes, for a toolbar of your own that calls `handle.api`. Theme colours in the canvas are read again when the theme changes. The canvas draws on demand (`frameloop="demand"`), only while the camera, a clip, a weight or a swap moves, and not at all while the stage is out of view or the tab is hidden. Without WebGL, or when loading fails (`labels.error`, announced at once), the poster stays with a message. `preloadModelViewer()` starts loading the scene chunk early; `sceneChildren` puts three.js content of your own inside the canvas, where `ModelViewerSceneContext` gives the viewer's handle and the model's rig. Agent calls before the model has loaded, or for a clip it doesn't have, throw with the reason.

items.name: model-scan
items.title: Model Scan
items.description: A photo becoming a 3D character, driven by an engine's events through props: landmark groups light up over the photo as meshes while the background dims around the person (from the engine's mask, or a hull around the pose landmarks), the person's pixels fly as a point cloud onto the base model while the camera turns, a shimmer reveals it and a pulse runs across the floor, streamed weights reshape it, and it hands over to orbit. Floating glass controls follow the stage: a style picker and Make 3D, a progress ring with Cancel, a toolbar of views, the clip, Download and Start over, and the error with Try again. Reduced motion crossfades instead. Announces each stage; agents get start, cancel, retry, restart and download.
items.docs: `<ModelScan src alt width height stage points masks model weights scaledWeights targetNames expressions progress statusText error onStart onCancel onRetry onStartOver onDownload styles selectedStyle onStyleChange controls modelAlt idleClip aspectRatio fit viewer actions labels>`: `stage` is `photo`, `detecting`, `building`, `refining`, `ready` or `error`: the UI's, which you map from your engine's. `points` light up while detecting: one list (a Float32Array of interleaved x, y fractions of the original photo, or `{ x, y }` objects), or groups `{ source, points, aspect?, edges? }` (the face, the body) that each light up on their own, in the order their sources arrived, a later group replacing its source's; `edges` (pairs of point indices) join a group into a mesh, and a `body` group of the 33 pose landmarks has the pose skeleton by default. They land straight on the photo where the stage draws it, following `fit` (`contain`, or `cover` in a stage of another `aspectRatio`); points past 0 or 1 are kept but not drawn. `masks` are the engine's person masks, `{ source?: "face" | "body", width, height, data }` (`data` a Uint8Array of 0-255 confidence, row-major from the top left, the photo's aspect): the body mask, or one of the photo's aspect, dims the background around the person while detecting and picks the pixels that fly onto the model; without one, a hull around the body's 33 pose landmarks stands in, and without those every pixel flies. `model` is the base GLB with morph targets, from `building` on: a URL, its bytes, or `{ glb, targetNames }`; the final character fades in over it keeping the weights. `weights` and `expressions` ease as they stream. At `building` the photo moves into the 3D scene exactly where the 2D photo was, then the person's pixels fly on curved, staggered paths onto points sampled over the model's surface, turning the info colour mid-flight and the surface's own as they land, a shimmer runs down the body revealing the model, the background's pixels drift out of focus, and a pulse runs across the floor, while the camera turns to the three-quarter view: one draw call, uniforms per frame. Under reduced motion the photo crossfades into the model. The controls float over the stage (`controls="overlay"`, the default) or sit under it (`"below"`): over the photo the style picker (`styles` of `{ value, label }`, `selectedStyle`, `onStyleChange`) and Make 3D (`onStart`); while working a progress ring, the stage's label (`statusText`), Step n of 4, the percent and Cancel (`onCancel`); over the finished model the style picker and a toolbar of views, the clip (`labels.play`), Download (`onDownload`) and Start over (`onStartOver`), icon buttons with tooltips; at `error` the message (`error`) with Try again (`onRetry`) and Start over. Each shows only with its callback; `actions` adds your own. All copy is in `labels`. The model's viewer takes drag and keys without a bar of its own (pass more of its props through `viewer`, like `floor={false}`). Screen readers hear each stage, progress at most every tenth and two seconds, and the error at once. Agents call `start`, `cancel`, `retry`, `restart` and `download`; a call the stage doesn't offer, or the app refuses through `details.cancel()`, fails the step with why.

items.name: attachments
items.title: Attachments
items.description: AttachmentStrip: a horizontally scrolling strip of image thumbnails and file chips (icon, name, type and size). Images open a Lightbox, files open their link, max adds a +N button. AttachmentThumb renders one. Agents get openAttachment(id).
items.docs: Each attachment is { id, name, kind: "image" | "file", src, srcDark?, thumbnail?, thumbnailDark?, alt, href?, size?, mimeType? }. Dark variants are rendered beside the light ones and CSS shows the one that matches the theme (`.dark`, or the system preference unless the page opted into light), so there is no flash. `onOpen(attachment, details)` runs before anything opens, for people and agents (`details.source === "agent"`); `details.cancel()` keeps it closed. Sizes are formatted with Intl in `locale`. The strip needs an `aria-label`; the other labels are English and overridable through `labels` (`open`, `more`, `lightbox`). Focus returns to the thumbnail that opened the lightbox.

items.name: file-input
items.title: File Input
items.description: UI SDK FileInput styled as a drop zone with a browse button: accept, size and count limits, the chosen files as attachment chips with remove buttons, and why any were left out in the destructive tone.
items.docs: `<FileUpload title description browseLabel accept maxSize minSize maxFiles multiple validate name labels locale>` inside a `Field`: the field's label names the browse button (the field's control), drops, pastes inside the zone and the picker all go through the same checks, the chosen files show as `AttachmentThumb` chips (name, type, size from `formatFileSize`) with a remove button each, and rejected files are listed under the zone with their first reason (`labels.rejected`). `title`, `description` and `browseLabel` are your copy; `labels` (`list`, `remove`, `rejected`) default to English. Compose the parts (`FileInput`, `FileInputDropzone`, `FileInputTrigger variant size`, `FileInputFiles`, `FileInputRejections`, `FileInputList`, `FileInputItem`, `FileInputItemRemove`) for a button alone, a page-wide drop (`target="document"`) or a folder (`directory`). The value is `File[]`, so `FormField` binds it as is. With `name` it submits through a native file input.

items.name: stage-track
items.title: Stage Track
items.description: Where a piece of work is in a configurable pipeline (branch, PR, dev, prod): StageTrack shows every stage in a row, reached ones filled and the current one emphasised, or only the current one as a StagePill. StageFilter is a toggle group with a count per stage.
items.docs: Stages are { id, label, tone? } with the shared Tone vocabulary; a stage without a tone uses the primary colour, and StagePill defaults to info. `current` is a stage id; stages before it count as reached. The track is an ordered list with `aria-current="step"` on the current stage, and each state has its own marker shape (check, ring, hollow), so meaning never rests on colour; give it an `aria-label`. Below a 24rem container it stacks into a column. `getHref(stage)` makes a stage a link. StageFilter is a UI SDK ToggleGroup (several stages by default, `multiple={false}` for one): nothing pressed means no filter, which a segmented control can't express. Agents set it with `setValue` and stage ids.

items.name: row-navigation
items.title: Row Navigation
items.description: One tab stop over a collection's rows on UI SDK roving focus: arrows and j/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter opens, Space and x toggle. Adds no role.
items.docs: `useRowNavigation({ ids, onOpen, onToggle, reveal })` makes the instance; wrap the rows in `RowNavigationProvider handle` and each row (a `tr`, or a row's link or button) in `NavigableRow id render`. `ids` lists every row in order, rendered or not, so Home, End and PageDown reach rows a virtualized collection hasn't rendered: `reveal(id)` scrolls one into view and focus follows when it renders. Enter calls `onOpen` only for rows that aren't links or buttons, which open themselves. Keys typed in a control inside a row stay with that control. Agents don't see it: the rows' parts and the collection's own actions already cover them.

items.name: virtual-rows
items.title: Virtual Rows
items.description: Windowed rendering for long lists and tables on UI SDK's virtualizer, in document flow with gap rows: it renders again only when the rows in view change, keeps the focused row rendered, and keeps find in page working through UI SDK's findable layers.
items.docs: `useVirtualRows({ count, virtualize, estimateSize, getKey })` virtualizes past 200 rows with `virtualize="auto"`. Put `anchor` on the `ul` or `tbody`; it scrolls with the nearest scrolling ancestor, or the window. Render `segments`: rows, and gaps (`aria-hidden`) that hold the space of the rows between, so a table keeps `tbody > tr` and a list `ul > li`. Give each row `data-index` and `ref={measureElement}`. `pin(index)` keeps the focused row rendered when scrolled away; `renderNow(index)` renders one at once, for an agent's action. Pass `findable: (index) => text` (stable) and UI SDK's findable layers hold the text of the rows that aren't rendered in `hidden="until-found"` stand-ins, so find in page reaches them and scrolls the real row in. Keep `getKey` stable (`useCallback` over the ids).

items.name: trail-rows
items.title: Trail Rows
items.description: The rows of a long trail or tree, shared by commit-history and git-tree: virtual-rows in document flow by default, or UI SDK's virtualizer with findable layers so find in page reaches rows that aren't rendered.
items.docs: `useTrailRows({ count, estimate, getKey, text, findable })` returns `segments` (rows, with a `top` when `absolute`, and gaps that hold the space of the rows between), `anchor` (the rows' parent, in flow), `setScroller` (the scroller), `measure`, `textSlot`, `pin`, `scrollToIndex` and `reveal`. Without `findable` it is `useVirtualRows` from `virtual-rows`, rows in document flow; with it, `useFindableRows` puts rows on UI SDK's virtualizer, absolutely positioned in a box `height` px tall, and builds its findable layers once the page is idle, so find in page reaches rows that aren't rendered by the pieces `text(index)` returns. `useInstanceState(instance)` reads a UI SDK primitive instance's state with `useSyncExternalStore`. `commit-history` and `git-tree` install it; you rarely need it directly.

items.name: list-item
items.title: List Item
items.description: Dense, Linear-style rows that also work as entity cards: List, ListGroup (label and count), ListItem with leading, title, subtitle, status, meta, trailing and actions, row actions that keyboards and agents reach without selecting the row, plus ListItemTitle, ListItemMeta, ListItemActions and IconTile. Agents get select(id), and run(id) per row action.
items.docs: `List aria-label` holds `ListItem`s, optionally inside `ListGroup label count`. The name goes on the list itself: a `ul` (`role="list"`), or the listbox when rows are selectable, with no group around it. A row selects through a stretched link (`href`, `aria-current="page"` when `selected`) or a stretched UI SDK Button (`onSelect`), and its actions, chips and status stay their own targets. Give `List` a `value`, `defaultValue` or `onValueChange` and the rows become options of a UI SDK Listbox (arrow keys, one tab stop); options can't hold controls, so `actions` are ignored there (use `rowActions`). `variant="card"` lays rows out as cards in a responsive grid. Titles wrap to two lines, then show the full title in a tooltip; a status pill wraps below a narrow title, and trailing content and actions drop to their own line on a narrow row. `List onSelect(id, details)` runs before a row is chosen, for people and agents, and `details.cancel()` stops it. Agents see the list by its label with `select(id)`; a selectable list also shows its listbox under the same name with `setValue`, and each action resolves to one of them. Rows of a non-selectable list are one tab stop: arrows or j/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter opens the row through its link or button, and the moved-to row scrolls into view with the least scrolling; a selectable list takes j/k and the page keys as its own arrows. Pass `items` with `renderItem` (and `getItemId`, `itemText`) to render rows from data, or give a row list `ListItem id` children directly (each child an element with a string `id`; `title` is its text), which the list reads as the same data: past 200 rows (`virtualize="auto"`, `estimateSize`) only the rows in view render, with `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`, every row reachable by keyboard and by agents' `select`, and find in page through hidden stubs. `checkedIds` with `onCheckedIdsChange` checks rows for a bulk action: Space or x toggles the focused row, each row shows a checkbox outside the tab order (`checkLabel` names it). `sortable` with `onReorder(ids, details)` reorders the rows of a non-selectable list from data: each row gets a drag handle named after its title (`sortableLabels`), the row's link or button keeps its own tab stop, checked rows move together, and agents get `move` and `reorder` on a sortable named like the list. A sortable list renders every row instead of virtualizing. `rowActions={(id) => ListRowAction[]}` gives rows actions that run without choosing the row, also in a selectable list or a MasterDetail: the list becomes an APG layout grid (`role="grid"`, rows with a primary cell, the row's link or button, and one `gridcell` per action), still one tab stop. Up/Down and j/k move between rows in the same column (clamped to a row's last cell), Left/Right (following the text direction) between a row's cells, Home/End to a row's ends and with Ctrl/⌘ to the grid's corners, Page Up/Down by a screen; Enter or Space presses the focused cell. Selectable, rows carry `aria-selected` and only the primary column selects (an arrow onto it or a press), never an action. A `ListRowAction` is `{ id, label, icon, onAction(details), href, newTab, disabled, confirm, tone }`: `id` is shared by the rows that offer it, an `icon` makes an icon button with the label in a tooltip, `onAction` runs for a press and an agent and `details.cancel()` refuses it, `href` makes it a link, `disabled` (true or why) keeps it focusable with the reason in its tooltip, `confirm` is its `data-agent-confirm` sentence and `tone: "destructive"` colours it. On a fine pointer the actions show while the row is hovered, focused or selected (`rowActionsVisibility="always"` keeps them), always on touch, each with a 44px hit area. Agents see one component per action, named by its label (`rowActionLabels.group`), whose `run(id)` takes a row's id, rendered or not; the rows' own buttons stay out of the snapshot. A row that doesn't offer it, a disabled one or a cancelled run fails the step with why. `ListGroup` becomes a `rowgroup` named by its label. With `sortable`, row actions are plain buttons. MasterDetail's `followFocus` ignores focus on a row's actions.

items.name: tree
items.title: Tree
items.description: UI SDK Tree styled as indented rows with guide lines: a file explorer from paths with folder and file icons, checkable trees with mixed branches, lazy branches, links and a flat list for virtualizing.
items.docs: `<Tree aria-label paths>` (or `items`) renders every row for you: an indicator, `checkable` checkboxes, an icon from `icon` (`treeFileIcon` by default: open or closed folders, file icons by extension; a function of the item and its state, or `false`) and the label. Compose `TreeItem` > `TreeItemLabel` (+ `TreeItemIndicator`, `TreeItemCheckbox`) and `TreeGroup` yourself, or `TreeNodes items icon checkable`, to render your own rows while the tree keeps the whole hierarchy. Rows indent by `--tree-level` and each open group draws a guide through its parent's indicator. Selection (`mode`, `value`, `activation`), expansion (`expanded`), checks (`checked`, `checkStrategy`) and `onAction` are UI SDK's; `toggleTreeItem(items, checked, value, strategy)` computes a checked value you keep yourself. Items with `href` render as links that follow on press (`onFollow` for a client router). For thousands of rows, keep `items` on the tree and render only the rows in view from `visibleTreeRows(items, expanded)`, scrolling in `onHighlight`; every item sets `--tree-level`, so flat rows indent the same.

items.name: side-panel
items.title: Side Panel
items.description: A non-modal inspector beside a list: a named complementary region, Escape closes it and returns focus to the row, shortcuts declared inside run while it is open, and on narrow screens it stacks below the list, overlays it or opens as a bottom sheet.
items.docs: `<SidePanel open onOpenChange title description actions returnFocus>` renders nothing while closed. Lay it out beside the list in a flex row (`--side-panel-width`, 24rem by default). `actions` (a status pill, small buttons) sit beside the title until the title would get narrower than `--card-heading-basis` (11rem), then wrap below it, as `CardHeader`'s do; the close button keeps its corner. `narrow` sets what happens at the `narrow:` breakpoint (760px and below): `"stack"` (default) keeps it in the page flow, full width, and makes its flex parent wrap so it goes below the list; `"overlay"` covers its positioned parent, as it always did before; `"sheet"` opens it as a modal bottom `Drawer` that takes focus and returns it to `returnFocus()` on close. `stack` is the default because it is the only mode that neither hides the page nor traps focus, so a panel that is open on load still leaves the list readable and reachable. Use `overlay` to show the panel instead of the list (a tall scroller in a bounded column, as the `inbox` block does), and `sheet` for a detail that should read as a step away from the list. Escape anywhere on the page closes it (a modal above it gets Escape first), and focus that was inside it, or lost to the body, moves to `returnFocus()`. It is a `ShortcutScope` that is active while open (`scope`, `scopeLabel` for the `ShortcutsDialog`), so `Button shortcut="u"` inside it works while focus stays in the list. `labels={{ close }}` names the close button.

items.name: lint-rules
items.title: Lint Rules (optional)
items.description: Optional oxlint config for Eskais UI consumers: the React, React Compiler and spacing-token presets of @p-otero/oxlint-rules, the @shadcn/lint design-system rules, eskais/icon-button-needs-label (an icon-only Button or Toggle takes size="icon" and an aria-label, so it shows a tooltip) and eskais/scroll-area as a warning (a bare overflow-auto or overflow-scroll class: scroll in a ScrollArea). Extend it from your .oxlintrc.json.

items.name: markdown-view
items.title: Markdown View
items.description: Renders Markdown (CommonMark, GFM tables, tasks and strikethrough, [[wikilinks]] and ![[embeds]]) to React elements with the Lezer parser, fenced code as a highlighted CodeBlock: raw HTML shows as text, only http, https, mailto and tel links become links, leading YAML frontmatter is hidden or shown as properties, and each top-level block is memoised so long notes re-render only what changed. Also extractHeadings for an outline and parseFrontmatter.
items.docs: Wikilinks: `resolveWikilink(target)` returns `{ exists, label }` (an unresolved link is dashed), `wikilinkHref(target)` its address, and `onWikilinkClick(target, event)` takes plain clicks and agents' `follow` for client routing (modified clicks stay with the browser). A wikilink with an address renders through `Link`, so it follows on press and hash routes (`#/note/x`) work; one without an address but with `onWikilinkClick` is a button. Both carry `data-wikilink` (`link` or `embed`) and `data-target`. Embeds: `![[target]]` and `![[target|alias]]` render `renderEmbed(target, alias)`, as a block when the embed is alone in its paragraph; without it, a dashed link-like chip. Frontmatter: a `---` block on the first line, closed by `---` or `...`, is hidden by default (`frontmatter="hide"`), a `<dl>` of its `key: value` lines and lists with `frontmatter="properties"` (named by `frontmatterLabel`, "Properties"), or its YAML with `"raw"`; `renderFrontmatter({ raw, properties, from, to })` draws your own. `parseFrontmatter(markdown)` reads it without a YAML dependency: plain `key: value` lines, `- item` and `[a, b]` lists, `|` and `>` blocks; nested maps are skipped, and `raw` is there for a real YAML parser. `extractHeadings(markdown)` lists `{ level, text, slug, line, from, to, textFrom }`, frontmatter and code left out, for an outline. `slug` is unique in the document (GitHub's rule: lowercased, punctuation dropped, spaces as `-`, `-1`, `-2`… after a repeat, `heading` for an empty one), and the view puts the same slug on each rendered heading as `data-slug`, so a filtered list still finds its heading. Keep the callbacks stable (module-level or `useCallback`): a new function re-renders every block. Images reserve their box before they load when their size is known: write it in the alt text as Obsidian does (`![A chart|640x360](chart.png)`, or `|640` for the width), or answer `imageSize(src, alt)` with `{ width, height }`; without either, the text below moves when the image arrives.

items.name: markdown-editor
items.title: Markdown Editor
items.description: A Markdown editor on CodeMirror 6 with a Typora-like live preview: the document is the Markdown text, so loading and saving keep every byte. Marks show only while the caret is inside their span; headings, bullets and quotes never show theirs; tables render as tables off the caret; frontmatter stays as written. Slash and [[ menus, a one-row toolbar with an overflow menu, a ref handle for host menus and outlines, English and Spanish labels, and agent actions (getMarkdown, insertText, replaceSelection, insertWikilink, toggleFormat, setHeading, toggleTask; setMarkdown needs approval).
items.docs: The value is plain Markdown: `value`/`onChange` (debounced by `changeDelay`, 300 ms; flushed on blur and unmount) or `defaultValue`. Loading never fires `onChange`. A `value` that arrives while edits are still waiting for `onChange` calls `onConflict({ local, remote })`: return the text to keep, or nothing to take the remote; without it the local text goes out through `onChange` first and then the remote applies. A `ref` gets a `MarkdownEditorHandle` once the editor mounts (`null` before): `focus()`, `getValue()`, `getSelection()` and `setSelection(anchor, head?)` in offsets of the Markdown string, `insertText(text, { userEvent }?)` (a plain `"input"` edit by default; `"input.type"` counts as typing, so a `[[` or `/` it inserts opens its menu), `openWikilinkSuggestions()` (focuses the editor, types `[[` unless the caret already follows one, and opens the wikilink listbox; `false` without `suggestWikilinks`), `insertWikilink(target, alias?)`, `insertLink(href, text?)`, `wrapSelection(before, after?)`, `runCommand(name)` for the toolbar's and the slash menu's commands, typed as `MarkdownEditorCommand`: formats, levels and blocks (`bold`, `quote`, `taskList`, `heading2`, `paragraph`, `codeBlock`, `table`, `divider`; any other name throws a RangeError), `insertBlock(kind)` for a block in place of the selection, as the slash menu inserts it (one implementation for both), `scrollToLine(line)` and `getScrollLine()`; writes return `false` when read-only, and no CodeMirror type is part of it. Line commands (toolbar, slash menu, handle) leave the caret after the marker they add. Wikilinks and `![[embeds]]`: Ctrl/Cmd+click, or Enter inside one, calls `onWikilinkClick(target, event)` (and `onOpenWikilink(target)`); `embedPreview` shows an embed off the caret as `renderEmbed(target, alias)` or a placeholder. A leading `---` YAML block stays as written, in a muted monospace block, and the caret starts on the line after it (`initialCaret="start"` for the very start; read at mount). `frontmatter="readonly"` protects it: an edit inside the block or across its fences keeps only the part outside it, and typing before the opening fence is dropped, so a whole note passed as `value` round-trips byte for byte; a new `value` still replaces it, for a properties panel of your own. The slash menu stays open with `labels.noMatches` while nothing matches, until Escape or a space. Code languages are opt-in: `npx shadcn add @eskais/markdown-editor-languages` and pass `codeLanguages={markdownCodeLanguages}`. The text scrolls in a `ScrollArea`: CodeMirror grows with it inside the viewport (`data-slot="markdown-editor-viewport"`) and still renders only the lines in view; size the editor with a height or a `max-h-*`. Pass `cspNonce` under a strict Content Security Policy (CodeMirror injects a style element). Spanish labels: `labels={markdownEditorLabelsEs}`. Shortcuts: Mod+B/I/E, Mod+Shift+X, Mod+Alt+0..6 for paragraph and heading levels, Tab/Shift+Tab to nest list items, Mod+Enter to toggle a task; Escape then Tab leaves the editor. Installing it also installs `@eskais/dropdown-menu` (the toolbar's menus: `DropdownMenu`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuItemIcon`, `DropdownMenuItemIndicator`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`), with `button`, `input`, `popover`, `scroll-area` and `tooltip`, into your `ui` folder. If you already have a `dropdown-menu.tsx` there, shadcn asks before overwriting it: keeping yours means the toolbar imports your file, so it must export those parts with the same props, or the editor breaks at build time. Add with `--overwrite`, or put your own menu under another name.

items.name: markdown-editor-languages
items.title: Markdown Editor Languages
items.description: Every code language CodeMirror knows, for MarkdownEditor's fenced code blocks; each language loads the first time a block names it. Opt-in, since the list adds about 230 KB of shared chunks to most bundles.

items.name: link
items.title: Link
items.description: Text link with inline, nav, muted, standalone and plain variants: underlined at rest or on hover so it never relies on colour, external and new-tab handling, aria-current, render for router links, an opt-in onFollow that routes plain clicks and gives agents a follow action, and fast navigation on a primary mouse press (fast={false} or data-no-fast-link to opt out); FastLinkRegion and useFastLink do the same for plain anchors.
items.docs: `onNavigate(href, event)` routes on the client on a press, a click or Enter, without the agent action `onFollow` adds; `onIntent(href)` runs on a 65 ms hover, focus or a mouse or pen press, to preload the route (idempotent: it can run more than once). Same-origin links follow on a primary mouse press (`pointerdown`), for navigation only: `fast={false}` opts a link out, `data-no-fast-link` on an ancestor a region or the app. Hash routers work too: an `href` that starts with `#/` follows on press, through `onFollow` or by setting `location.hash`, while any other `#…` href is an in-page anchor and stays native. Set another prefix with `data-fast-link-hash-prefix` on an ancestor (`<body data-fast-link-hash-prefix="#!/">`) or `FastLinkRegion hashPrefix`; an empty value makes every `#…` href an anchor.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: CodeBlock and CodeTabs: syntax highlighting for ts, tsx, js, jsx, json, css, html, bash, md and diff with Lezer parsers loaded on first use, rendered as React elements in syntax tokens that hold 4.5:1; a filename header, copy (an agent action too), line numbers, highlighted lines, wrap and a max height. Code for inline code.

items.name: diff
items.title: Diff engine
items.description: Line diffs with histogram (default, git's most readable for code) or linear-space Myers with a cost cut, git's slider placement, hunks with context and the enclosing-definition heading, whitespace options, binary and size guards; changed words or characters within a line; a unified-diff parser for multi-file git patches (renames, copies, modes, new, deleted, binary, quoted paths); and diffTextAsync, which runs in a Web Worker past 200k characters. No dependencies.
items.docs: `diffText(old, new, { algorithm, context, ignoreWhitespace, maxLines, maxChars })` returns `{ status, hunks, additions, deletions }`; its output matches `git diff --histogram` (or `--minimal` with `algorithm: "myers"`). `formatHunks(hunks)` prints them back as a unified diff. `parsePatch(text)` reads `git diff`, `git show` or `diff -u` output into `FileDiff`s. `intraline(oldLine, newLine, { mode: "word" | "char" })` gives the changed ranges, or null for a rewritten line. `diffTextAsync(old, new, { signal })` diffs in a Web Worker past `workerThreshold` (200k characters), on the main thread below it, without workers, or when a Content Security Policy refuses `blob:` workers: the worker is built from the engine's own source in a Blob, so it works in every bundler without a worker file.

items.name: ansi
items.title: ANSI
items.description: parseAnsi and stripAnsi read a line of terminal output in one linear pass: SGR codes (the 16 colours, 256 colours and truecolor in the semicolon and colon forms, bold, dim, italic, underline, inverse, strikethrough, reset) become styled runs, and every other escape sequence, OSC string (titles, hyperlinks), control character and bidi override is dropped; a carriage return redraws the line. The text comes back as strings, never markup. ansiCssColor maps a terminal colour to theme-aware CSS that clamps its lightness to --ansi-lightness-min and --ansi-lightness-max, for 4.5:1 on muted in light and dark.

items.name: diff-view
items.title: Diff View
items.description: The renderer behind TextDiff and GitDiff: every file's lines in one virtualized scroller (UI SDK createVirtualizer), unified or split, folded unchanged regions, changed-word highlights, Lezer syntax colours parsed in slices and applied only to the lines on screen, one tab stop over the lines (createGridFocus), j/k and n/p between hunks and files, Shift ranges for comments (onLineSelect), find in page across folded and off-screen lines, and agent actions.
items.docs: `<DiffView files={toViewFiles(fileDiffs)} headers />` with `layout`/`defaultLayout`/`onLayoutChange` (`unified`, `split`), `wrap`, `viewed`/`onViewedChange`, `defaultCollapsed`, `onLineSelect(selection, details)` (`{ path, start: { side, line }, end, lines }`, or null) and `intraline` (`word`, `char`, false). `createDiffViewController()` drives it from outside (`openFile`, `nextHunk`, `markViewed`, `setLayout`…). Labels are overridable (`diffLabels`, `diffLabelsEs`); pass a constant. `height="auto"` (default) grows to the whole diff and scrolls with the nearest scrolling ancestor (or the page), which the virtualizer follows; a `--diff-max-height` set by the page caps it and it scrolls inside past that. `height="fill"` fills a sized parent.

items.name: text-diff
items.title: Text Diff
items.description: Compares two strings: unified or split, line numbers, unchanged regions folded behind Expand N lines, changed words highlighted, syntax colours by language, word wrap, line selection and find in page; inputs past 200k characters diff in a Web Worker.
items.docs: `<TextDiff oldText newText language="tsx" />` takes the diff options (`algorithm`, `context`, `ignoreWhitespace`, `worker`, `workerThreshold`) and every DiffView prop. Small inputs diff during render; large ones in a worker, with `loading` shown before the first result and `aria-busy` while a newer one computes.

items.name: git-diff
items.title: Git Diff
items.description: A patch or a list of file diffs for review: per-file headers (rename arrow, status chip, +/- counts and bar, mode change, collapse, viewed), a tree of changed files to jump between them, unified/split and wrap controls, one virtualized document for 500-file patches, j/k and n/p, line selection for comments, and agent actions openFile, nextHunk, previousHunk, markViewed and getHunk.
items.docs: `<GitDiff patch={gitDiffOutput} />` or `files={fileDiffs}` (give `oldText`/`newText` to make unchanged regions expandable). `fileTree` and `toolbar` default to true; the tree hides on narrow screens. Marking a file viewed folds it. `onViewedChange` and `onLineSelect` report what the reviewer did; `details.source === "agent"` tells an agent's change apart. GitDiff fills its parent (`height="fill"`), so give it a height; binary files and mode-only changes show `labels.binaryFile` or `labels.modeChange` instead of counts.

items.name: hero
items.title: Hero
items.description: The top of a landing page: an eyebrow chip, a title with an optional muted second line, a description, actions, a copyable install command and an aside for a live demo, side by side or centered by container width, over a token-drawn grid or glow.

items.name: section-heading
items.title: Section Heading
items.description: The heading of a page section: eyebrow, a large title, a description and actions, start-aligned or centered, with the heading level and id the enclosing section names itself by.

items.name: bento
items.title: Bento
items.description: Bento and BentoTile: a container-query grid of Card tiles that spans columns on wide containers, falls to two columns and then one, and can make a whole tile a link without covering the controls inside.

items.name: steps
items.title: Steps
items.description: Steps and Step: an ordered list with numbered markers, a title, a description and any content per step, side by side on wide containers and stacked on narrow ones.

items.name: site-footer
items.title: Site Footer
items.description: A page footer: brand, description, groups of links as named navigation landmarks, and a bottom line.

items.name: docs-layout
items.title: Docs Layout
items.description: DocsLayout, an app shell for documentation: a topbar slot, a sidebar that sticks under it at the full remaining height (a drawer on narrow screens), a breadcrumb slot above the page in the main column, the main landmark and a sticky table of contents. Also DocsToc (headings marked as you read with IntersectionObserver), DocsPager and DocsBreadcrumb.
items.docs: Compose the shell from a Topbar and a Sidebar that share one controller: `const sidebar = useSidebarState({ storageKey: "docs-sidebar" })`, then `<DocsLayout topbar={<Topbar leading={<SidebarTrigger {...sidebar.triggerProps} />} brand={…} trailing={…} />} sidebar={<Sidebar label="Documentation" {...sidebar.sidebarProps} collapse="hide" trigger={false} narrowQuery="(width <= 47.5rem)">…</Sidebar>} header={<DocsBreadcrumb items={…} />} toc={<DocsToc items={headings} />}>…</DocsLayout>`. The topbar sticks to the top; the sidebar sticks under it (`top: var(--topbar-height)`) at the full remaining height and scrolls on its own; elements with an `id` in the page scroll into view below the topbar. The trigger collapses the sidebar on wide screens and opens its drawer on narrow ones. Without a `topbar`, pass `--docs-top` in `style` to clear a fixed header of your own.

items.name: shell
items.title: Shell
items.description: Shell, an application's whole frame from its routes: a skip link, a Topbar (sidebar trigger, brand, ⌘K search, actions), a grouped Sidebar that sticks under it, collapses (remembered) and is a drawer on narrow screens, a command palette whose Go to group reaches every route, a MobileNav bottom bar with More on narrow screens, and the main landmark. Router-agnostic: onNavigate for a history router, #/route hrefs for a hash router, or plain fast links.
items.docs: `<Shell routes={routes} groups={[{ id: "main", label: "Workspace" }, { id: "legacy", label: "Legacy", tone: "muted" }]} currentHref={pathname} onNavigate={(href) => router.push(href)} brand={<Logo />} actions={<UserMenu />} storageKey="app-sidebar">{page}</Shell>`, with `routes` of `{ id, label, href, icon?, group?, mobile?, placements?, keywords?, badge? }` (extend the type with your own fields: `onNavigate` gets your route back). `currentHref` is an href or a matcher `(href) => pathname.startsWith(href)` (the longest match wins); it sets `aria-current="page"` and the primary fill in the sidebar, the bottom bar and the palette. Without `onNavigate` routes are plain links that fast links follow on press, and `#/route` hrefs work with a hash router. Routes flagged `mobile: true` (up to four) fill the bottom bar on narrow screens and More opens the rest; `mobile: { order: 1 }` orders the bar apart from the sidebar (by `order`, then list position; `true` is order 0); `placements` (`"sidebar"`, `"mobile"`, `"more"`, `"palette"`, all by default) limits where a route shows, and decides over `mobile`: without `"mobile"` it stays out of the bar, and listing it puts the route in the bar; the bar is sticky at the end of the shell, so the page always ends above it. Translate every string with `labels` (`skipToContent`, `sidebar`, `mobileNav`, `goTo`, `more`, `openSearch`, `search`, `empty`…). Add palette commands with `commandGroups` (CommandGroups) and run them with `onCommand`. `searchFooter` goes at the bottom of the palette, for key hints in your language. The palette's Go to commands are links to the routes' hrefs (Ctrl/Cmd+click opens a new tab); following one closes the palette and goes through `onNavigate`.
