Each open of the palette starts with an empty search and one Escape closes it; `searchQuery`/`onSearchQueryChange` control the search and `defaultSearchQuery` starts each open. `sidebarShortcut="mod+b"` (opt-in) toggles the sidebar, or opens its drawer on narrow screens. `useShellSidebar()` inside the Shell returns its `useSidebarState()` result (`collapsed`, `setCollapsed`, `controller`); to hold it outside, call `useSidebarState({ storageKey })` yourself and pass it as `sidebar`. `sidebarHeader` and `sidebarFooter` go above and below the sidebar's routes. `main="fill"` (or a route's `main: "fill"` while it is current) gives `<main>` the height left under the topbar and above the bottom bar, so a `DocumentWorkspace` or any `h-full` page fills it and scrolls inside; no wrapper sized with `--shell-column-height`. Put pages in `PageLayout` (not `as="main"`: the shell owns `<main id="main">`). Inside a pane, set `--shell-height` in `style` to the pane's height and pass `as="div"` if the page already has its `<main>`.

items.name: landing-page
items.title: Landing Page
items.description: A whole landing page made only of blocks (Hero, SectionHeading, Bento, Steps and SiteFooter, with a header slot), with its content in one object: the template to copy and edit.

items.name: icon
items.title: Icon
items.description: Icon names a lucide-react icon (or any SVG component) for screen readers: <Icon icon={TrashIcon} label="Deleted" /> renders role=img with that label. Decorative icons need no wrapper, since lucide hides them by default.
items.docs: The registry draws its icons with `lucide-react`: import them by name (`import { CheckIcon } from "lucide-react"`). Lucide sets `aria-hidden` on an icon that has no `aria-*`, `role` or `title` prop, so a decorative icon needs no wrapper. Use `Icon` only when the icon carries meaning nothing else states: `<Icon icon={TriangleExclamationPointIcon} label="Blocked" />` renders `role="img"` with that `aria-label`. Size comes from the parent (Button, Badge, menu items and inputs set `[&_svg]:size-4`) or a `size-*` class: `size-3.5` beside `text-body-sm`, `size-4` beside `text-body`, `size-5` beside a title; our classes override lucide's `size` prop. Colour is `currentColor`: set a text colour, like `text-success`.

items.name: conversation
items.title: Conversation
items.description: A chat or agent thread: a role="log" that follows new messages while the reader is at the end, stops when they scroll up and shows a "new below" pill that jumps back (smooth unless reduced motion), keeps a streaming message in view, loads older messages above without moving the view, and server renders. ConversationMessage is an article named by its author, with avatar, relative time and data-from (user, assistant, agent, system, tool); ConversationComposer composes Textarea and Button. Agents read messages and call jumpToLatest.
items.docs: `<Conversation label="Thread with Atlas" composer={<ConversationComposer onSend={send} />}>{messages.map((m) => <ConversationMessage key={m.id} messageId={m.id} from={m.from} author={m.author} avatar={…} time={m.at} now={now} streaming={m.streaming}>{m.text}</ConversationMessage>)}</Conversation>`. Give it a bounded height (it fills its parent). It renders every message: keep a window of the newest few hundred in state and pass `hasOlder` and `onLoadOlder` (add the older ones in one update) for longer threads. A streaming message sets `aria-busy`, so screen readers read it once it is whole. `useConversation()` inside it returns `jumpToLatest`, `release` and `loadOlder`. Labels (`newBelow(count)`, `jumpToLatest`, `loadOlder`, the composer's `message` and `send`, and the screen-reader names per role) are overridable.

items.name: activity-log
items.title: Activity Log
items.description: Who changed what, and when, with undo: createActivityLog records the page's UI SDK control changes (from people, agents and the app) and the app's own records, and steps back and forward through them. ActivityLog lists them newest first; pressing an entry seeks to it, Undo and Redo bind Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z outside text fields, and undoToast shows a toast with Undo. Agents call undo, redo and seek; a seek that undoes more than confirmAbove entries needs a person (data-agent-confirm).
items.docs: Create the log once in the browser, with the app's agent bridge, before the controls render: `const log = createActivityLog(agent, { within, describe })`. Then `<ActivityLog log={log} label="Activity" header={…} />`. `log.record({ label, description, actor, undo, redo })` adds a change of the app's own, like a task an agent moved. `log.undo()`, `redo()`, `seek(n)` (0 is the start) and `undoActor("agent")` resolve with what they couldn't put back; restoring goes through the bridge, so permissions and change callbacks still apply, and a password, card or one-time-code field is never put back. It wraps UI SDK's experimental history helpers behind its own types. Entries read UI SDK's English sentences unless you pass `describe`; every label is overridable.

items.name: log-viewer
items.title: Log Viewer
items.description: LogViewer: a live log or terminal output viewer for any process. createLogStore takes lines from anywhere (append, or write for raw chunks with partial lines) into a bounded buffer and notifies once per frame; the viewer renders only the lines in view, on UI SDK's virtualizer inside a ScrollArea. It follows the end until the reader scrolls up, then shows Jump to end with a count of new lines (End or the button follows again); filters by source (a ToggleGroup, sources coloured with chart or tone colours) and by search; renders ANSI colours on theme tokens; marks error lines (by level or an isError pattern) and steps through them with F8 and Shift+F8; copies the shown lines or a selection as plain text; wraps on demand. A role=log with aria-live off and a polite status that announces new errors at most every 5 seconds. Agents read the shown lines and call filter, search, nextError, previousError, copy, jumpToEnd and setWrap.
items.docs: Create the store once, outside render: `const store = createLogStore({ maxLines: 10000 })`. Feed it from anywhere: `store.append({ text, source: "backend", level: "error", time })` for whole lines, or `store.write(chunk, { source })` for a process's raw output (partial lines wait for the rest, colours carry across lines per source). Then `<LogViewer store={store} label="Environment output" sources={["frontend", "backend", { id: "db", label: "postgres" }]} timestamps />` in a box with a height (`className="h-96"` or `min-h-0 flex-1`). `isError={/ERR!|Exception/}` marks lines without a level; `hiddenSources`, `query` and `wrap` can be controlled with their `on…Change`; `format` writes a line for copy and agents; `actions` adds toolbar buttons; `toolbar={false}` hides the toolbar. Every label is overridable through `labels`.

items.name: inbox
items.title: Inbox
items.description: A keyboard-first inbox block: a virtualized List of messages, j/k and Enter to open a SidePanel inspector with single-key actions, x to select for a bulk action and ? for every key.

items.name: master-detail
items.title: Master Detail
items.description: MasterDetail: a list with a detail pane, side by side on wide containers and stacked below 42rem with a Back button. Controlled or uncontrolled selection, optional URL sync through a router-agnostic adapter (hash routers included), j/k that follow focus, a detail that collapses to a rail or resizes, remembered under a storageKey, and focus that moves to the detail's heading and back to the row. Agents open and close items by the block's name.
items.docs: `<MasterDetail label="Devices" renderList={(state) => <List aria-label="Devices">{devices.map((d) => <ListItem key={d.id} title={d.name} {...state.itemProps(d.id)} />)}</List>} renderDetail={(id) => ({ title, description, actions, content })} emptyDetail={<Empty … />} />`. It fills its parent's height (`--master-detail-height`, 100% by default), so give it a bounded box, like an app shell's main column; in a page that scrolls, `height="auto"` sizes it to its content between `--master-detail-min-height` (16rem) and `--master-detail-max-height` (40rem) with the panes scrolling inside, instead of a hard-coded height (to fit what is left of the window, set the max from your app's own CSS). `idleDetail="visible"` keeps `emptyDetail` (a monitor, a summary) under the list on containers under 42rem, capped at `--master-detail-idle-height` (50%), with a button that collapses it to its bar (beside the list too with `collapsible`); `emptyDetailTitle` titles that bar and names the pane. `selectedId`, `defaultSelectedId` and `onSelectedIdChange` (cancel with `details.cancel()`); `url={createUrlParam("device")}` from `@/lib/url-param` keeps it in the URL (`{ in: "hash" }` for a hash route's query, `{ router: hashRouter() }` to go through a `UrlRouter` from `url-router` or your router's own API); for a route of your own shape (`#/devices/<id>`), control `selectedId` from the route instead; `followFocus` opens the row that j/k move to, but not a row whose action takes focus (give the `List` `rowActions` for Open, Copy or Start buttons on a row); `collapsible`, `resizable` and `storageKey` for the detail's width. Every label is in `labels`.

items.name: dashboard-grid
items.title: Dashboard Grid
items.description: DashboardGrid: a row of stats over a container-query grid of cards (one column, two from 42rem, `columns` from 64rem) where rows are at least one height and cards in a row share it, so they line up, keep their size from loading to loaded and grow their row rather than clip. DashboardCard spans columns and rows and loads through DataState (a skeleton, the error with Retry, an empty title); DashboardChart fills a card and is named by its title; DashboardMeter centres a ring meter in one; DashboardStats and DashboardStat (with a StatDelta in `delta`) draw placeholders of the value's height.
items.docs: `<DashboardGrid columns={3} labels={{ errorTitle, emptyTitle }} stats={<DashboardStats aria-label="This week" loading={pending}><DashboardStat label="Runs" value={261} delta={<StatDelta value={0.12} comparison="vs. last week" />} loading={pending} /></DashboardStats>}><DashboardCard title="Runs" span={2} status={query.status} data={query.data} error={query.error} onRetry={query.refetch}>{(data) => <DashboardChart config={config}><BarChart data={data}>…</BarChart></DashboardChart>}</DashboardCard></DashboardGrid>`. Rows are at least `--dashboard-row-height` (20rem) tall and cards in a row share the height; a card whose content is taller grows its row, never clips it, so set the row height to fit your cards to keep loading and loaded the same height. Without `status`, a card shows its children as they are; `DashboardMeter label value hint` centres a ring meter in it. `retry`, `loading` and `refreshing` default to English and every label is overridable on the grid or a card.

items.name: settings-page
items.title: Settings Page
items.description: SettingsPage: a section navigation that sticks beside the sections on wide containers and becomes a section picker on narrow ones, marking the section being read (IntersectionObserver). Going to a section scrolls by id and focuses its heading, so it works under hash routers; the section can live in the URL through createUrlParam. SettingsSection, SettingsRow (a label, a description and the control on the right, stacking when narrow), SettingsFacts (a DescriptionList for read-only facts) and SettingsDangerZone with SettingsDangerAction rows that confirm through ConfirmDialog and need a person's approval for agents.
items.docs: `<SettingsPage url={createUrlParam("section")} style={{ "--settings-top": "var(--topbar-height)" }}><SettingsSection id="security" title="Security" description="…" actions={…}><SettingsRow label="Two-factor authentication" description="…"><Switch /></SettingsRow></SettingsSection><SettingsSection id="device" title="This device"><SettingsFacts aria-label="This device"><DescriptionItem>…</DescriptionItem></SettingsFacts></SettingsSection><SettingsDangerZone id="danger" title="Danger zone"><SettingsDangerAction label trigger title confirmLabel agentConfirm onConfirm disabled pending /></SettingsDangerZone></SettingsPage>`. The navigation lists every direct `SettingsSection` child with a text title (`navLabel` otherwise), or pass `sections`. `--settings-top` is the height of anything sticky above the page and `--settings-height` the box that scrolls it. `currentSection` and `onSectionChange` (reason `scroll`, `nav` or `url`) follow your own state. The navigation's links take their href from the `url` adapter (`createUrlParam("section", { router: hashRouter() })` gives `#/settings?section=id`, which opens the right route in a new tab), else `#id`; `getHref` overrides it, and `navigation="buttons"` renders buttons that only scroll, for sections with no address. A `SettingsRow` is a `Field` that names a UI SDK control; `field={false}` for a button. Labels `nav` and `jump` are overridable.

items.name: auth-page
items.title: Auth Page
items.description: AuthPage: a centred, brand-led page for signing in, registering from a one-time link and recovering an account, with a logo, a title, a description, one primary action, other options, an alert slot and footer links. `status` (idle, working, error, success) marks the action pending and announces `workingLabel` while a ceremony such as WebAuthn is open, shows the error in a live destructive Alert with a retry, and swaps the actions for a success slot. It holds no auth logic.
items.docs: `<AuthPage logo={<Brand />} title="Sign in" description="…" status={status} action={{ label: "Sign in with a passkey", icon: <KeyRoundIcon />, onAction: signIn }} workingLabel="Waiting for your passkey" error="The passkey request was cancelled." retry={{ label: "Try again" }} success={<Alert tone="success">…</Alert>} secondary={<Button variant="link">Recover your account</Button>} footer={<><Link href="/terms">Terms</Link>…</>} />`. Put fields (a name, a recovery code) in `children`, between the description and the action, and a note for any status (who invited you, when the link expires) in `alert`. `working` gives the action `loading` (a spinner, `aria-busy`, presses ignored while it keeps focus) and reads `workingLabel` once, politely; `error` shows `error` in an `Alert tone="destructive" live` whose retry runs `retry.onRetry`, or the action again; `success` replaces the action and `secondary` with `success`. The card is at most `--auth-page-width` (26rem) wide and the page at least `--auth-page-height` (100dvh) tall, padded clear of the safe areas, so it fills a phone at 390px. Every visible word comes from you: there is no default copy.

items.name: account-menu
items.title: Account Menu
items.description: AccountMenu: the signed-in user in a Shell or topbar. The trigger shows an avatar (or initials) and the name, which hides on narrow screens; the menu has a header with the name, email and an optional role Badge, your app entries (Devices, Security, Invite) and sign-out, which can ask first through ConfirmDialog, whose confirm then needs a person's approval for agents.
items.docs: `<Shell actions={<AccountMenu user={{ name, email, avatarSrc }} roleLabel="Admin" items={[{ value: "devices", label: "Devices", icon: <MonitorSmartphoneIcon />, onSelect: () => router.push("/devices") }]} signOutLabel="Sign out" onSignOut={signOut} confirmSignOut={{ title: "Sign out?", confirmLabel: "Sign out now", agentConfirm: "Signs you out of this device" }} />} />`. It goes in the Shell's `actions`, the topbar's end, which stays put whether the sidebar is a rail, hidden or a drawer, or in any Topbar's `trailing`. An item's `onSelect` that returns a Promise keeps it pending and the menu open until it settles, and so does `onSignOut`. Agents press the trigger with an item's text (`press` with "Devices"); with `confirmSignOut`, the dialog's confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm`, so an agent's sign-out waits for your `allow` (the mark sits on the button that confirms, not on the menu item that opens the dialog, so a person is asked once). `labels.trigger(name)` names the trigger ("Account: Ana Ruiz" by default).

items.name: invitation-panel
items.title: Invitation Panel
items.description: InvitationPanel: an admin creates an invitation and gets a one-time link, shown once with a copy button, a live expiry countdown that switches to expired, and a revoke behind a confirmation; below, the pending invitations with role, creator, expiry and revoke, through DataState. Agents can create, copy and revoke, and never read the link.
items.docs:
`<InvitationPanel aria-label="Invitations" roles={[{ value: "editor", label: "Editor" }]} invitations={pending} status={status} onRetry={refetch} onCreate={({ role }) => api.invite(role)} onRevoke={(id) => api.revoke(id)} text={{ create: "Create invitation", newLink: "New invitation link", expiresIn: (time) => <>Expires {time}</>, createdBy: (name) => `Created by ${name}`, … }} />`.

**The link is shown once.** `onCreate` resolves to `{ id, url, expiresAt }`, and the URL appears in one place only: the new link view, right after it resolves. The panel keeps it in memory, out of its state, and forgets it when the view is dismissed, when the link is revoked or expires, and when the panel unmounts. It never writes it to the address, storage, a `data-*` attribute, a `title` or any `aria-*` text. The pending list's `Invitation` type has no `url`, so your API never has to hand a link out again: a lost link is revoked and a new one created. Keep the URL out of your own logs and state too.

**Agents never read it.** The URL sits under `data-agent-hidden`, so it is left out of the agent snapshot, `query` and every `act` result, and announcements only say a link was created or copied. Agents see the new link in the panel's state as `link: { id, expiresAt, expired }`. `create(role?)` takes a role's value or label and resolves to `{ id, expiresAt }`; `copy()` writes the URL to the clipboard and resolves to `"copied"`. UI SDK's bridge doesn't wait for a promise, so an agent's step reports both as `pending` and reads `link` and `copied` from the next snapshot. `copy` fails with why when no fresh link is held (dismissed, expired, revoked) or the page has no clipboard. `revoke(id)` opens the confirmation for a pending invitation or the new link; its confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.revokeAgentConfirm`), so the revoke waits for a person, and an unknown id fails the step. The pending invitations are the panel's agent items, by id.

The countdown is a RelativeTime that ticks by the second in the last two minutes. Expiry takes one timeout per boundary, none while the page is hidden, and checks the clock when the page shows again. The pending list's loading, empty and error states come from DataState (`status`, `error`, and `onRetry` with `text.retry`). Every visible word comes from `text`, with no default; `labels` holds the screen-reader names and announcements, in English by default.

items.name: eskais-mockup-skill
items.title: Mockup skill
items.description: Agent skill for @eskais/mockup: build a throwaway, offline HTML mockup of a screen from the project's own components in five levels (project components, uninstalled registry items, parts, UI SDK primitives with a reason, recorded gaps), validate it and present every screen as images, with a gallery. Lands in .agents/skills/eskais-mockup.
items.docs: The skill runs the mockup CLI with Bun 1.4 from `.agents/tools/eskais-mockup`, the `eskais-mockup-cli` item: add both with `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/eskais-mockup-skill @eskais/eskais-mockup-cli`. Codex and Cursor read `.agents/skills` as it is. Claude Code reads `.claude/skills` instead: link the folder with `mkdir -p .claude/skills && ln -s ../../.agents/skills/eskais-mockup .claude/skills/eskais-mockup`, or on Windows, in PowerShell, `New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path .claude\skills\eskais-mockup -Target .agents\skills\eskais-mockup`.

items.name: eskais-mockup-cli
items.title: Mockup CLI
items.description: The mockup CLI the eskais-mockup skill runs: inspect the project's components, build a screen into one offline HTML file, validate it and write a gallery of its screenshots. Bun 1.4 or newer runs it from .agents/tools/eskais-mockup with no npm dependencies; it reads the project's components.json, stylesheet and tsconfig.
items.docs: Run it from the project root with Bun 1.4 or newer: `bun .agents/tools/eskais-mockup/cli.ts inspect`, then `validate <name>`; `--version` prints the release it came from. It needs a TypeScript project (`tsx: true` in components.json): shadcn renames `.ts` files to `.js` in a JavaScript project, and Bun can't run them. The folder starts with a dot, so TypeScript's `include` globs leave it out of the app's type-check and build; a linter that walks every file still reads it, and it passes Vite's ESLint config and `lint-rules`. Update it with the registry: `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/eskais-mockup-cli --overwrite`.

items.title: Performance skill
items.description: Agent skill that keeps Eskais screens fast: virtualized rows instead of thousands of mapped ones, effects in hooks, React Compiler-friendly code, transform and opacity motion, fast links for navigation only, blur kept off large animated surfaces, and measuring with the React Profiler and the Performance panel. Lands in .agents/skills/eskais-perf.

items.name: eskais-ui-skill
items.title: Eskais UI skill
items.description: Agent skill for building with Eskais UI: which component to reach for, install and aliases, forms, lists and navigation, styling tokens, data display, toasts and testing, and the AgentTaskBoard. Lands in .agents/skills/eskais-ui; load it with the ui-sdk skill.
items.docs: Codex and Cursor read `.agents/skills` as it is. Claude Code reads `.claude/skills` instead: link the folder with `mkdir -p .claude/skills && ln -s ../../.agents/skills/eskais-ui .claude/skills/eskais-ui`, or on Windows, in PowerShell, `New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path .claude\skills\eskais-ui -Target .agents\skills\eskais-ui`. The skill builds on UI SDK's own `ui-sdk` skill, which ships in `node_modules/@ui-sdk/core/skills/ui-sdk`: `cp -r node_modules/@ui-sdk/core/skills/ui-sdk .agents/skills/`.

items.name: document-workspace
items.title: Document Workspace
items.description: A notes or docs workspace: an explorer, tabs, breadcrumb, toolbar, the document (edit or read), an aside for backlinks, properties and the outline, a status bar with the save state, an alert slot and Ctrl/Cmd+P quick open. Resizable, collapsible columns when its container is wide, drawers when narrow; named landmarks and toggles agents can press. Also DocumentOutline and DocumentQuickOpen.
items.docs: `<DocumentWorkspace document={mode === "edit" ? <MarkdownEditor ref={editor} …/> : <MarkdownView …/>} explorer tabs breadcrumb toolbar statusBar aside alert quickOpen={<DocumentQuickOpen items onOpen />} mode onModeChange editorRef={editor} headings={extractHeadings(markdown)} saveState storageKey>`. It fills its parent (`--document-workspace-height`, 100% by default) and decides its layout from its own width, never the viewport, so it works inside an app shell's `<main>` (in a `Shell`, give it `main="fill"` or the route `main: "fill"` and it fills the height left): at `narrow` (760 px) or less, the explorer and the aside are 20rem drawers that start closed; wider, they are resizable columns (`Resize files`, `Resize details` handles) that collapse from their toggles or the handle. `explorerOpen`/`onExplorerOpenChange` and `asideOpen`/`onAsideOpenChange` follow what is shown, and control it; turning narrow closes them and turning wide brings back the columns. A link in the explorer drawer closes it; pass `documentId` (the open document's slug or path) and the drawer also closes when it changes, whatever opened the document: a button in your tree, quick open, a wikilink or an agent. `useDocumentWorkspace().closeExplorer()` closes the drawer from your own tree (the wide column stays). `storageKey` remembers the columns' state and widths in localStorage (the drawers always start closed). Landmarks: the explorer is a `nav`, the aside an `aside`, the document a named region (`documentAs="main"` when the workspace is the page's main content); the toggles carry `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The mode switch is a SegmentedControl; switching keeps the reading position by heading (from the editor's `getScrollLine` to the read view's headings and back). `saveState` (`saved`, `saving`, `unsaved`, `error`) is a polite `<output>` in the status bar; `alert` sits in an assertive region that is always there, so a conflict is read once when it appears (pass an `Alert` without `live`). `quickOpen` adds a Quick open button and `quickOpenShortcut` (`mod+p`, `false` to turn it off). `DocumentQuickOpen` searches in one of two ways. With `items`, it filters them in the browser by label and `keywords` (`filter`: `"fuzzy"` by default, `"contains"`, `"startsWith"` or a function); for a search of your own, pass `filter={false}`, `onQueryChange` and `status` (`"loading"`, `"error"`) and set `items` from its results, which are then listed as they are, so a note that matched on its body shows although its title lacks the query. With `source` (a `PageSource<T, { q?: string }>` from `@eskais/page-source`, as `ServerCombobox` takes) and `getItem`, it searches the server itself while it is open: the query goes out as `filter.q` once typing pauses (`debounce`, 200 ms), a newer query aborts the request in flight, the server's order is kept and the next page (`pageSize`, 20) loads at the end of the list. Loading and errors show in the list and are read out; `labels` takes `empty` (text or a function of the query), `loading`, `error` and `count`. `DocumentOutline` lists `headings`: in edit mode an entry puts the caret at the heading (`setSelection`, `scrollToLine`) and focuses the editor; in read mode it scrolls to the heading and focuses it, found by its `slug` (the `data-slug` `MarkdownView` renders), so a filtered `headings` list, like one without empty headings, still reveals the right one; `useDocumentWorkspace().revealHeading(heading)` does the same for your own outline. Drawers, quick open and menus give focus back to the document unless the action moved it: pass `useDocumentWorkspace().documentFocusTarget` as `finalFocus` to your own menus in `toolbar`. `editorRef` takes any `DocumentEditor` (`focus`, `scrollToLine`, `setSelection`, `getScrollLine`), which `MarkdownEditorHandle` is. All text is in `labels`.
